title: Benchmark leaves sockets and ack loops running on any error, so a failed run hangs instead of exiting
test: tests/benchmarkRuntime.test.js: 'benchmark closes its sockets and exits 1 when the warm-up metrics request fails', 'benchmark stops its acknowledgement loops, closes its sockets and exits 1 when sampling fails mid-run', 'benchmark closes the sockets that did connect and exits 1 when one connection is refused' (written by TASK-043)
proof: Already fixed by TASK-043 (commit d0a126b), so TASK-048 changed nothing for this issue and only re-checked it. The three failure paths of the issue are the three tests above: a refused connect among several clients, a failing warm-up fetchMetrics, and a failing fetchMetrics in the sampling loop with the ack loops running. Each runs scripts/benchmark-runtime.js as a child process against a local http + socket.io fixture and asserts that the process exited by itself (not killed after 10 s), exit code 1, the failure message on stderr, zero sockets still connected on the fixture, that every socket that had connected ended with the server-side reason 'client namespace disconnect' (the script closed it, it was not dropped with the process), and for the mid-run case that acknowledgements had been flowing. Re-proved here against the script as it was before TASK-043 (git show d0a126b^:scripts/benchmark-runtime.js put in place, TASK-043's tests unchanged): all three failed with AssertionError 'the harness should exit by itself: true !== false' (the open sockets kept the event loop alive and the test had to kill the process after 10 s). With the current script all three pass. The script now connects with Promise.allSettled, registers each socket when it is created, and runs connect, warm-up and sampling inside try/finally that sets running=false, waits for the ack loops (bounded: ack timeout + interval + 1 s) and then closes every socket. The prompt's step 2 asks to close the sockets first and then await the loops; TASK-043 awaits the loops first on purpose, and that is right: checked with a scratch socket.io client, closing a socket while an acknowledgement is in flight calls its callback with 'socket has been disconnected', which would make the last in-flight acknowledgement of a successful run count as a failed one in the summary. A run against a stopped server (--url=http://127.0.0.1:9) prints 'Benchmark failed: websocket error' and exits 1 after 0.2 s.

title: Benchmark validates required load only at the final sample
test: tests/benchmarkRuntime.test.js: 'benchmark fails when the required load is missing in earlier samples even though the last sample has it', 'benchmark reports the lowest observed load of the window and passes when every sample meets the requirements'; tests/runtimeBenchmarkModel.test.js: 'observeTopology reads the load of one metrics sample and counts a missing field as 0', 'topology samples [ok, ok, ok] pass and report the lowest value of each requirement', 'topology samples [ok, under-loaded, ok] fail and name the sample where the requirement was first unmet', 'topology samples report every unmet requirement in the order of the final-sample check', 'relay bytes stay a whole-window total and are not required of each sample', 'topology samples without any sample fail every requirement and report no minimum'
proof: On the unchanged code the harness test ran the benchmark against a fixture whose metrics report no mediasoup consumers in sample 2 and no producer in sample 3 while the last sample has both: the run exited 0 with pass true (AssertionError 'Expected values to be strictly equal: 0 !== 1' on the exit code), which is the issue's pass with a topology that was missing mid-window. The second harness test failed because summary.topologyMinimums did not exist (actual undefined), and the six new model tests failed with TypeError because observeTopology and evaluateTopologySamples did not exist. After the fix: observeTopology(metrics) reads one sample's rooms, producers, consumers, viewers, relay viewers and fallback pipelines (a missing field counts as 0, so a requirement for it still fails); evaluateTopologySamples(samples, requirements, windowTotals) checks the rooms, producers, consumers, relay viewers and fallback pipelines requirements against every sample collected after the startup discard (the section Q-004 default) and returns { failures, minimums }; each failure names the first unmet sample, for example 'required 5 mediasoup consumers in every sample, lowest observed 1, first unmet at sample 2 of 4 (2026-10-24T12:00:01.000Z)'. relayBytesForwarded stays the whole-window delta between the first and last sample and is checked once with its old message. The benchmark prints the minimums as the new summary field topologyMinimums; summary.topology keeps its keys and still shows the last sample plus the whole-window relay total. Samples [ok, under-loaded, ok] fail and [ok, ok, ok] pass (model tests); a complete-metrics run still exits 0 with the summary on stdout (existing test 'benchmark with complete metrics reports measured values and passes' passes unchanged). evaluateTopology (single snapshot) is unchanged and its existing test passes; the benchmark no longer calls it. Threshold checks and headroom output are unchanged.
